topic: Options slider reliability and SFX test control
currentUserGoal: Do a small Grass Touching Simulator redesign slice while waiting for new model availability, focusing on the still-rough Options/SFX controls.
workCompleted: Added a visible Test SFX button to the redesign Options panel and exposed it through the DOM agent layer as redesign-sfx-test-button.
Changed redesign Options slider tracks, fills, and hit areas to use explicit sizes instead of scaled rectangles so visual state, pointer math, and DOM bounds align better.
Stopped option-panel controls from propagating pointerdown into the backdrop close handler, and added pointerupoutside cleanup for slider drags.
Made the panel itself interactive so clicking inside empty panel space does not accidentally close Options.
Hid native browser range visuals for the transparent DOM sliders while preserving a focus outline for keyboard/agent accessibility.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 30 Vitest tests, TypeScript, and Vite production build.
Started Vite on http://127.0.0.1:5173 and loaded http://127.0.0.1:5173/?redesign&playtest in the in-app browser.
Opened Options through redesign-options-button and verified one music slider, one SFX slider, and one Test SFX button were present.
Set music to 45% and SFX to 55% through DOM range controls; documentElement dataset state reported musicVolume 0.45 and sfxVolume 0.55.
Clicked Test SFX and checked browser console errors; none were reported.
Visually inspected the Options panel screenshot after hiding native range visuals; the custom sliders remained visible without the browser-native blue slider overlay.
knownIssues: The in-app browser domSnapshot API errored with incrementalAriaSnapshot during this check, so targeted locator/evaluate checks were used instead.
The Options panel is functionally cleaner, but the broader redesign still needs user playtesting for feel and visual nostalgia.
The focus outline can appear around the invisible DOM range when automation focuses it; this is intentional for accessibility, but real mouse use should mostly show the custom Phaser slider.
nextRecommendedSteps: Ask the user to test Options in a normal mouse flow: open Options, drag Music/SFX, click Test SFX, close, reopen, and confirm values persist.
If the focus outline is visually distracting during normal use, narrow it to keyboard-only behavior or restyle it as a subtler glow around the Phaser track.
Continue the next gameplay slice after the user confirms the Options controls feel reliable.
doNotRevert: Keep the separate SFX volume setting and Test SFX affordance; the user values grass-touch sound feedback.
Keep DOM-accessible options controls for agent/browser testing.
Do not reintroduce native range visuals over the Phaser sliders.
